elicitation_input.question: What are the differences between Acute myeloid leukemia and Chronic myeloid leukemia?
elicitation_input.question_type: Summarization of information on a topic

llm_generation.text:
# Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) vs Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML)

## Cell of Origin & Maturation Arrest
- **AML**: Malignant transformation of myeloid progenitor cells with a block in differentiation—cells arrest at the **blast** stage. Blasts accumulate and fail to mature into functional granulocytes, monocytes, etc.
- **CML**: Originates from a pluripotent hematopoietic stem cell, but cells largely **retain the ability to differentiate**. You see a full spectrum of myeloid maturation (myeloblasts through mature neutrophils), just in excessive, dysregulated numbers.

## Genetic Driver
- **AML**: Heterogeneous. Common mutations/translocations include **FLT3-ITD, NPM1, CEBPA, t(8;21) RUNX1-RUNX1T1, inv(16) CBFB-MYH11, t(15;17) PML-RARA** (APL), and others. No single unifying genetic lesion.
- **CML**: Defined by the **Philadelphia chromosome, t(9;22)(q34;q11)**, producing the **BCR-ABL1 fusion gene**. This fusion protein has constitutive tyrosine kinase activity, driving proliferation. Present in >90-95% of cases.

## Clinical Course
- **AML**: Aggressive, rapidly progressive (days to weeks). Presents with symptoms of marrow failure—**anemia, thrombocytopenia (bleeding/bruising), neutropenia (infections)**—because blasts crowd out normal hematopoiesis.
- **CML**: Indolent, slow-growing, often **discovered incidentally** on routine CBC. Progresses through phases:
  - **Chronic phase** (median duration years, especially with TKI therapy)
  - **Accelerated phase**
  - **Blast crisis** (transforms into an acute leukemia, either myeloid or lymphoid)

## Peripheral Blood/Bone Marrow Findings
- **AML**: **≥20% blasts** in blood or marrow required for diagnosis (per WHO criteria). Auer rods may be seen (pathognomonic for myeloid lineage).
- **CML**: Marked **leukocytosis** (often >100,000/µL) with a **left shift showing the full spectrum** of granulocyte maturation—myelocytes, metamyelocytes, bands, segmented neutrophils. **Basophilia and eosinophilia** are characteristic. Blasts are typically <10% in chronic phase.

## Age & Epidemiology
- **AML**: Median age ~65-70 years, though it occurs across all ages (including a notable pediatric incidence). Associated with prior chemotherapy/radiation, myelodysplastic syndrome, certain genetic syndromes (Down syndrome).
- **CML**: Median age ~55-65 years. Less common in children.

## Leukocyte Alkaline Phosphatase (LAP) Score
- **AML**
